finding.title: Fix the Makefile check-15 awk pipeline so cross-feature deep-import detection can actually fire
finding.rule: Rule 0 / Rule 2 / AG-11 (a standard ships with a deterministic checker; checker failures print file:line and exit non-zero -- a check that structurally cannot fire is a broken guardrail)

evidence.quote: awk -F: '{match($$1, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, a); match($$0, /features\/([^\/]+)\//, b); if(a[1] != b[1]) print}'

finding.why: $1 (awk field 1, the file path column) and $0 (the whole grep output line, which starts with that same file path) are both matched against the identical regex `features/([^/]+)/` -- since the file's own path is always the leftmost occurrence of that pattern in $0 too, `a[1]` and `b[1]` are always extracted from the SAME text (the importing file's own feature folder), so `a[1] != b[1]` can never be true and the check prints nothing, always, regardless of what's actually imported. I reproduced the exact pipeline directly: the grep -P pre-filter stage alone finds 70+ candidate cross-feature import lines (including at least 10 genuine features/{dashboard,learning,notifications,sync,content_browsing}/** files deep-importing into features/gamification/**), but piping through the full check-15 awk command yields exactly 0 output lines. Unlike check 14 (which lists its ~32-edge backlog so it's at least visible for future cleanup), check 15 gives zero visibility into the Rule 2 backlog size today, and -- more importantly -- will never flag a brand-new cross-feature deep import added by any future change, even once the check is flipped from warn-only to enforcing.
finding.recommendation: Fix the awk script to compare the importing file's feature folder against the IMPORTED path's feature folder specifically (e.g. split $1 and the import-statement portion of $0 separately, or use two distinct match targets), then re-run make audit and confirm it lists the real backlog the way check 14 does.
acceptance_criteria: Running the check-15 pipeline against the current tree (unchanged) prints the real cross-feature deep-import edges instead of nothing
A synthetic new deep import added between two features is caught (non-zero WARN output) after the fix

finding.title: Replace hardcoded Color(0x...) literals with theme/AppColors tokens across gamification presentation widgets
finding.rule: custom_lint no_color_literal_outside_theme (currently non-functional since dart run custom_lint crashes; not covered by any make audit grep)
finding.why: 38 raw Color(0x...) literals across these 10 files bypass the design-token system entirely (contrast with achievement_unlock_celebration.dart:179-180, which correctly reuses AppColors.chartGreen/chartBlue in the same list). This is exactly the pattern the no_color_literal_outside_theme custom_lint rule exists to catch, but that lint currently can't run at all (custom_lint_core/analyzer version mismatch, already flagged by the orchestrator), so nothing today prevents new color literals from being added or flags the existing ones. Concrete cost: no single place to retheme/dark-mode this feature, and visually-identical colors (e.g. several near-duplicate blues/creams) are redefined independently per file instead of shared.
finding.recommendation: Extract the repeated literals into named constants in core/theme/app_colors.dart (or reuse existing ones where a near-duplicate already exists) and reference those from all 10 files; once dart run custom_lint is repaired, let no_color_literal_outside_theme enforce this going forward.
acceptance_criteria: No lib/features/gamification/**/*.dart file (excluding generated) contains a Color(0x...) literal outside core/theme
no_color_literal_outside_theme reports zero violations in this feature once custom_lint is functional again

finding.title: Delete or wire up the unreachable form.error branch in reward_configuration_screen.dart
finding.why: RewardForm.error defaults to null and is never set to a non-null value anywhere: RewardConfigController.bootstrap() explicitly sets `error: null`, and grep across the whole gamification feature finds no other `copyWith(error: ...)` call. The `if (form.error != null)` branch and its whole error Scaffold (lines 287-293) are therefore unreachable dead code -- a maintenance trap for the next person who assumes it's live error-handling.
finding.recommendation: Either delete the dead branch, or wire a real failure path (e.g. bootstrap()'s try/catch setting a localized error) that actually reaches it.
acceptance_criteria: Either the form.error != null branch is removed, or a test demonstrates a real code path setting it and rendering the error Scaffold

finding.title: Delete PointsPopupWidget or give it a real call site
finding.why: grep across lib/ and test/ shows PointsPopupWidget is only ever referenced from its own test file (points_display_widget_test.dart) -- it is never instantiated by any screen (not learning_screen.dart, not bulk_mark_screen.dart, nowhere completion-triggered popups would plausibly live). It's fully-formed, styled, and tested code that the app never actually shows to a user.
finding.recommendation: Either remove PointsPopupWidget and its test, or wire it into the completion-celebration flow it was clearly built for (alongside AchievementUnlockCelebration) and add a widget test proving it renders from a real screen.
acceptance_criteria: PointsPopupWidget is either deleted (with its test) or has at least one production call site exercised by a widget test

finding.title: Add .autoDispose to points_providers.dart's family providers
finding.why: Both are classic (non-@riverpod) family providers with no `.autoDispose` -- in this Riverpod version, a manually-declared provider not marked autoDispose is kept alive for the container's lifetime once first read. Because CurriculumId is a small finite enum, the leak is bounded (at most ~15-20 cached results per provider), so the practical memory cost is small, but it's inconsistent with every other parameterized provider this same feature declares (achievementsOverviewProvider, _pointConfigDataProvider, pendingRedemptionsProvider are all explicitly .autoDispose), suggesting an oversight rather than a deliberate choice.
finding.recommendation: Add `.autoDispose` to both curriculumPointsProvider and pointsHistoryProvider.
acceptance_criteria: Both family providers in points_providers.dart are declared with .autoDispose
